name: Appeal to Authority
shortDef: Treating someone's say-so as proof, especially outside their expertise.
definition: Accepting a claim because an authority figure endorses it when that person lacks expertise in the topic, speaks against the consensus of their field, or offers nothing beyond their status.
howToSpot: Is the authority an expert in this specific topic?
Do other experts in that field agree, or is this one voice?
Is there evidence behind the endorsement, or just a title or fame?
classicExample: A famous quarterback swears by these magnetic insoles, so they must fix back pain.
legitimateVersion: Relying on experts is reasonable when they speak within their field and reflect its consensus, like trusting independent structural engineers about a crack in your foundation.

contrast.fal_bandwagon: Appeal to authority leans on one esteemed source; bandwagon leans on how many people believe or do something.
contrast.fal_genetic_fallacy: Appeal to authority accepts a claim because of who vouches for it; the genetic fallacy judges a claim by its origin or history.
